areas.name: Amesbury Sports Park (formerly Amesbury Ski Tow)
areas.note: The Amesbury Ski Tow (two 1,500-ft tows on Powwow Hill, Amesbury) operated from before 1949 until the early 1990s and is defunct as a lift-served alpine ski area; the successor Amesbury Sports Park operates as a snow-tubing facility, not alpine skiing. Source: nelsap.org lost-ski-areas listing for Amesbury.

areas.name: Bellows Falls Ski Tow
areas.note: Also referenced as the Rockingham Recreation / Bellows Falls Village Area rope tow; NELSAP's dedicated page only confirms operation through the 1999/2000 season with no evidence of current operation, so treated as inactive/defunct.

areas.name: Blackwater Ski Area (Proctor Academy)
areas.note: Private school-owned area in Andover, Merrimack County. Per Wikipedia's Proctor Academy article, Blackwater Ski Area serves as the base for the school's student ski patrol; no source found establishing a published public lift ticket, so treated as school-only rather than open to the public.

areas.name: Blandford Ski Area
areas.note: Defunct. Former ski area in Blandford, Hampden County; owned by the Springfield Ski Club 1936-2017, then bought and reopened by Ski Butternut for 2018/19, but permanently closed as of a March 26, 2020 announcement. Source: Wikipedia (Blandford Ski Area).

areas.name: Brodie Mountain
areas.note: Defunct. Former ski area in New Ashford, Berkshire County, closed in 2002 after Jiminy Peak's owners acquired it in 1999; site later repurposed as a wind power installation. Source: Wikipedia (Brodie (ski area)).

areas.name: Caribou High School Ski Area
areas.note: Likely school-only. School-owned surface-lift (800-foot O'Connor handle tow) area operating since the 2004-05 season, per newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/caribouhigh.php, but that source does not state whether it sells public lift tickets, and no public-ticketing page could be located for it (Caribou's city recreation site was unreachable). Excluded on the presumption of school-only use, consistent with the comparable Kents Hill/O'Connor facility above; a later wave should confirm directly with Caribou High School / RSU 39 if this needs revisiting.

areas.name: Carter's XC Ski Center
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country only, no lift-served alpine terrain. Located in Bethel (786 Intervale Rd.); cartersxcski.com describes it as exclusively a cross-country ski, snowshoe, and fat-tire-bike center with no downhill/alpine skiing.

areas.name: Chapman Hill
areas.note: Also known as Williston Ski Associates; NELSAP's Vermont overview page flags it "(private)."

areas.name: Cosmic Hill
areas.note: Private ski hill in the Mad River Valley; NELSAP's Vermont overview page flags it "(private)."

areas.name: Craftsbury Outdoor Center
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country and biathlon training center in Craftsbury Common; operator's own site (craftsbury.com) markets skiing without reference to any alpine lift, consistent with its well-known identity as a Nordic-only center. No lift-served alpine terrain identified.

areas.name: Diamond Hill (Ski Valley / Diamond Hill Reservation)
areas.note: Defunct. Two successive ski operations on Diamond Hill in Cumberland: Ski Valley (1939-1981) and Diamond Hill Reservation (mid-1960s-mid-1980s); the hill is now a public park with hiking trails and athletic fields, no ski lifts. Source: Wikipedia (Diamond Hill (Rhode Island)).

areas.name: Dutch Hill
areas.note: Defunct southern-Vermont ski area; listed among closed areas in NELSAP's Vermont overview with no reopening noted.

areas.name: Easton Ski Area
areas.note: Private, chairlift-served ski area on the Pocumtuck Range in Deerfield, run by and for Eaglebrook School; explicitly 'closed to the public' per source, no public lift ticket. Source: Wikipedia (Pocumtuck Range and Easton Ski Area).

areas.name: Eaton Mountain
areas.note: Defunct/not operating. Former ski area in Skowhegan, Somerset County; last operated the 2018-19 season, with all operations suspended before the 2019-20 season and no confirmed reopening since. Source: newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/eaton.php.

areas.name: Pine Top Ski Area (Escoheag Hill)
areas.note: Defunct. Former ski area off Escoheag Hill Road in West Greenwich, opened 1965-66 with two T-bars and night skiing, closed around 1980; the lodge burned in the mid-1980s and the site is now part of Arcadia Management Area. Source: Wikipedia (Escoheag Hill).

areas.name: Evergreen Valley
areas.note: Defunct. Former ski resort in Stoneham, Oxford County; last operated the 1981-82 season, and the Finance Authority of Maine voted to close it in fall 1983 after a loan default. Lifts have been removed and the US Forest Service lease has long expired. Source: newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/evergreenvalley.php.

areas.name: Gilbert's Hill
areas.note: Defunct as a ski area (closed 1965), site of the first rope tow in the northeastern U.S.; per Wikipedia it is now a privately owned historic farm property in Woodstock with no operating lift, open to the public only via conservation/historic easements.

areas.name: Great Glen Trails
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country, snowshoeing and fat-biking center with no lift-served alpine terrain. Confirmed via greatglentrails.com, which lists only cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, fatbiking, tubing and a snowcoach -- no alpine ski lift.

areas.name: Harris Hill Ski Jump
areas.note: Active ski-jumping venue in Brattleboro (reopened 2009, FIS-certified 2011), but per Wikipedia it is exclusively a jumping hill with no lift-served downhill terrain open to the public.

areas.name: Hermitage Club at Haystack Mountain
areas.note: Private, member-owned club (Hermitage Club), not open to the public. Confirmed via a fetch of the Hermitage Club's own site/coverage describing 2025/2026-season leadership and membership as a private club; also flagged "(private)" for Haystack Mountain in Wikipedia's list of Vermont ski areas.

areas.name: Hogback Mountain
areas.note: Defunct; operated on natural snow only from 1946-1986 and closed. Per Wikipedia, the former ski area in Marlboro is now town conservation land with informally maintained trails and no operating lift.

areas.name: Jackson Ski Touring Foundation
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country trail network (50+ trails, 100km+) with no lift-served alpine downhill terrain. Confirmed via jacksonxc.org, which describes only groomed cross-country/skate-ski trails, rentals and instruction -- no chairlift or downhill runs.

areas.name: Maple Valley
areas.note: Defunct; NELSAP's Vermont overview lists it among closed southern-Vermont areas (Dummerston area) with a long-running "Buy the Mountain" effort and no confirmed reopening; not found operating on any current source checked.

areas.name: Mount Greylock Ski Club
areas.note: Listed as a private, members-only ski club near Williamstown/South Williamstown, Berkshire County, with no published public lift ticket. Source: skicentral.com Massachusetts ski-area listing, which flags it explicitly as private; no operator website or Wikipedia article could be located to independently confirm current operating status, so this row is unverified rather than fully sourced.

areas.name: Mount Prospect Ski Tow
areas.note: Not confirmed operating. Per Wikipedia's Mount Prospect Ski Tow article, this small state-leased tow within Weeks State Park (Lancaster, Coos County) last operated in 2021 and did not open for 2022-23 due to organizational and snowmaking issues; described as 'intermittently operated' with no source confirming it has resumed for 2026-27.

areas.name: Mount Rowe (Alpine Ridge)
areas.note: Defunct. Wikipedia's Mount Rowe article lists it in the category of defunct NH ski areas/resorts, describing the former Alpine Ridge/Mt. Rowe ski operation (and the original single-chair Gunstock lift, now removed) north of Gunstock Mountain, Gilford, Belknap County.

areas.name: Mount Tom Ski Area
areas.note: Defunct. Former ski area in Holyoke, Hampden County, closed in 1998 after 36 seasons; the abandoned lodge burned in a 2020 fire. Source: Wikipedia (Mount Tom Ski Area).

areas.name: Mount Watatic Ski Area
areas.note: Defunct. Small ski area on Mount Watatic in Ashburnham, Worcester County, operated from the 1930s until closing in 1984; a 1988 reopening attempt as 'Ski Adventure' also failed. Now conservation land. Source: Wikipedia (Mount Watatic).

areas.name: Mount Whittier Ski Area
areas.note: Defunct. Wikipedia's Mount Whittier article describes it as 'a former ski resort,' listed in Wikipedia's category of defunct NH ski areas.

areas.name: Notchview
areas.note: A Trustees of Reservations property in Windsor, Berkshire County, operated exclusively as a 40-kilometer Nordic/cross-country ski trail system with no lift-served alpine terrain. Source: Wikipedia (Notchview).

areas.name: O'Connor Alpine Training Center
areas.note: Private. The Joanne and Dick O'Connor Alpine Training Center in Readfield is the private ski area of Kents Hill School, used for the school's competitive ski teams and student programs; not sold as a public lift ticket. Source: newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/kentshill.php, which describes it explicitly as "the private ski area of the Kents Hill school."

areas.name: Osceola Playground
areas.note: Small municipal rope-tow ski hill operated by the City of Pittsfield (Parks & Recreation / Community Services) in Pittsfield, Berkshire County, Massachusetts, running mainly weekends when snow conditions permit, with no snowmaking. Distinct from Bousquet Mountain, which is also in Pittsfield and is already a build row in this roster. Facility existence, public/municipal nature, and town/county are well sourced (nelsap.org's dedicated Osceola Playground page and NELSAP's Massachusetts overview), but current-season (2026-27) operation could not be independently confirmed -- the City of Pittsfield's own site returned 404s/redirects during this check, and no corroborating local news was found. Dropped rather than built on that basis; revisit to confirm operation before building.

areas.name: Pete's Tow
areas.note: Family-owned private rope tow (the Gebbie family) in Greensboro; NELSAP flags it as a private family tow, not a publicly ticketed area.

areas.name: Pine Mountain
areas.note: Former ski area in Goshen; NELSAP's overview lists it as reopened but explicitly notes it is now "a private ski area," not open to the public.

areas.name: Pineland Farms Nordic Skiing
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country only, no lift-served alpine terrain. Located in New Gloucester; pinelandfarms.org lists cross-country skiing and snowshoeing as its winter activities with no alpine/downhill or lift offering.

areas.name: Plymouth Notch
areas.note: Listed "(private)" in Wikipedia's list of Vermont ski areas; no public lift-ticket operation identified.

areas.name: Potanipo Hill
areas.note: Defunct. Per Wikipedia's Potanipo Hill article, the ski area closed in 1984; the former slopes in Brookline, Hillsborough County now host the Andres Institute of Art.

areas.name: Quechee Ski Area
areas.note: Small ski hill within the private, membership-based Quechee Club/Quechee Lakes community; Wikipedia's list of Vermont ski areas flags it "(private)" and the Quechee Club's own site (members-only club) returned a 403 when fetched, consistent with restricted access.

areas.name: Rangeley Lakes Trails Center
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country only, no lift-served alpine terrain. Described on its own materials (rangeleylakestrailscenter.org and rangeleymaine.com) as a multi-use trail system of roughly 50km for Nordic skiing, fat biking, and snowshoeing, with no mention of an alpine lift.

areas.name: Rikert Outdoor Center
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country-only center on Middlebury College's Bread Loaf campus in Ripton; per Wikipedia it offers cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and fat-biking with no lift-served alpine terrain.

areas.name: Round Top
areas.note: Former ski area near Plymouth Union; NELSAP lists it as reopened under the name Bear Creek Club, but bearcreekclub.com now redirects to a GoDaddy "domain for sale" parked page, indicating the successor operation is no longer active.

areas.name: Snow Valley
areas.note: Defunct; per NELSAP's dedicated Snow Valley page, the Winhall-area resort closed permanently in 1984 and its abandoned lift infrastructure remains on site, used only informally by hikers/snowmobilers today.

areas.name: Sonnenberg at Twin Farms
areas.note: Ski slope on the grounds of Twin Farms, an exclusive private resort property in Barnard; NELSAP flags it as a private/exclusive-club-type property, not open to the general public.

areas.name: Temple Mountain Ski Area
areas.note: Defunct. Per Wikipedia's Temple Mountain Ski Area article, it operated 1938-2001 and closed after the 2000-01 season; straddled Temple and Peterborough, Hillsborough County.

areas.name: The Balsams
areas.note: Closed to the public since 2011. Per Wikipedia's Balsams Resort article, as of 2024 it remains under long-running redevelopment (Les Otten-led, Goldman Sachs financing) with no operating ski lifts open to the public; not an operating ski area for 2026-27.

areas.name: Timber Ridge
areas.note: Defunct; per NELSAP's dedicated Timber Ridge page (Windham area), the area closed in 1991 and "there are currently no plans to reopen this area" despite some early-2000s restoration activity.

areas.name: Trapp Family Lodge
areas.note: Nordic/cross-country-only touring center in Stowe; per Wikipedia it offers cross-country ski trails but no lift-served alpine terrain.

areas.name: Tuckerman Ravine
areas.note: No lift of any kind -- skin-up/hike-to backcountry terrain reached via the Tuckerman Ravine Trail from Pinkham Notch. Confirmed via Wikipedia's Tuckerman Ravine article, which describes only foot access and no ski lifts.

areas.name: Weston Ski Track
areas.note: Cross-country ski and snowshoe area in Weston, Middlesex County, sited on the Leo J. Martin Golf Course; no lift-served alpine terrain. Source: Wikipedia (Weston Ski Track).

areas.name: Woodbury Ski Area
areas.note: Defunct. Former ski area in Woodbury, Litchfield County, closed in 2016 following a drought and has not reopened for skiing, despite a subsequent property sale. Source: Wikipedia (Woodbury Ski Area).

areas.name: Mohawk Mountain Ski Area
areas.note: Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Mohawk Mountain Ski Area), listed under Connecticut's currently-operating ski areas; located in Cornwall, Litchfield County.

areas.name: Mount Southington
areas.note: Base area is in the Plantsville village of the incorporated town of Southington, Hartford County (Plantsville is not itself an incorporated municipality). Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Mount Southington), status listed 'Operating'.

areas.name: Powder Ridge Mountain Park & Resort
areas.note: Originally opened 1959 as 'Powder Hill'; closed 2007-2013 amid ownership/financial trouble, reopened for skiing in January 2014 under Brownstone Exploration & Discovery Park as Powder Ridge Mountain Park & Resort. Confirmed currently operating via Wikipedia (Powder Ridge Ski Area); located in Middlefield, Middlesex County.

areas.name: Ski Sundown
areas.note: Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Ski Sundown), located in New Hartford, Litchfield County; replaced its Exhibition Triple chairlift with a new Skytrac quad for the 2024-25 season, indicating active ongoing investment.

areas.name: Baker Mountain
areas.note: Small volunteer-run community area operated by the Baker Mountain Ski Tow Club. newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/bakermtn.php headers the area as "Bingham, Maine" but notes it sits "just off US 201 north of Bingham and Moscow" and serves both towns; both Bingham and Moscow are in Somerset County so the county is not in doubt, but a later wave should confirm the exact town line before publishing. Confirmed open for 2025-26 ($20 weekend ticket) with recent Feb 2026 condition reports. Town corrected from Bingham to Moscow: the Town of Moscow, Maine's own site states outright that "Moscow is home to Baker Mountain Ski Tow, one of the oldest ski areas in the state" (moscowmaine.org), while the Town of Bingham's official site does not mention the ski area at all. newenglandskihistory.com, the research file's source, only places it generically "north of Bingham and Moscow" without choosing a side. Somerset County is unchanged -- both towns are in it.

areas.name: Big Moose Mountain (Big Squaw)
areas.note: Also marketed historically as Squaw Mountain/Big Squaw Mountain Resort; ski area is on Big Moose Mountain near Greenville, Piscataquis County (newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/squawmtn.php and Wikipedia list of US ski areas both give Greenville). Reopened its triple chair in 2013 under Friends of Squaw Mountain, which leases the area for $1/year from owner Confalone; a December 2024 fundraiser was announced to try to acquire the mountain outright. 2025-26 lift tickets were priced and sold ($50 adult weekend), opening Dec 27. Ownership/lease situation should be re-checked by a later wave before publishing operating details, since it has a history of near-closures.

areas.name: Big Rock
areas.note: Non-profit, transferred from Maine Winter Sports Center to a local non-profit in fall 2013. Located Mars Hill, Aroostook County. Confirmed operating 2025-26 (Dec 12 - Mar 22 season) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/bigrock.php.

areas.name: Black Mountain of Maine
areas.note: Non-profit, run by the Black Mountain Operating Board after Maine Winter Sports Center transferred it in 2013; hosts biathlon. Located in Rumford, Oxford County. Confirmed operating 2025-26 ($65 weekend ticket) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/blackmtn.php.

areas.name: Camden Snow Bowl
areas.note: Municipally owned and operated by the Town of Camden, Knox County. Confirmed operating for 2025-26 ($60 weekend ticket, Dec 13 opening) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/camdensnowbowl.php.

areas.name: Hermon Mountain
areas.note: Located in Hermon, Penobscot County. Confirmed operating 2025-26 ($55 daily, $520 season pass, Dec 13 - Mar 19) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/hermonmtn.php, which also notes the area was sold to new ownership as of May 8, 2026 - a later wave should confirm the new owner's name.

areas.name: Lonesome Pine Trails
areas.note: Non-profit community area in Fort Kent, Aroostook County, with an alpine T-bar (installed 1985-86) plus snowmaking and night skiing, distinct from the adjacent Fort Kent Outdoor Center nordic trails. Confirmed currently operating via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/lonesomepine.php.

areas.name: Lost Valley
areas.note: Located in Auburn, Androscoggin County. Confirmed currently open and operating via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/lostvalley.php, with a March 15, 2026 conditions report and a March 2026 note about the operator "considering terrain and lift expansion." (Note: this area has previously been reported elsewhere as having closed circa 2019-2020; the ski-history source's dated 2026 condition reports indicate it is running again/still running this season, so a later wave should double check current ownership before publishing.)

areas.name: Millinocket Ski Slope
areas.note: Town-driven revival of a 1950s-era rope tow near Stearns High School; Millinocket's town manager pursued grant funding starting 2022 to "bring the ski tow back to life," and the rebuilt rope tow debuted February 27, 2026, per newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/millinocket.php. That source does not spell out formal admission/ticketing policy - a later wave should confirm public access terms and the facility's official name before writing guide copy.

areas.name: Mount Abram
areas.note: Independently owned community-focused resort, located in Greenwood, Oxford County. Confirmed operating for 2025-26 (Dec 20 - Mar 29 season) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/mtabram.php.

areas.name: Mount Jefferson Ski Area
areas.note: Located in Lee, Penobscot County. newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/mtjefferson.php lists 2025-26 status as Open with $44.99 tickets, but also logs an August 2026 news item that the ski area has been placed on the market for $3.5 million and a January 2026 item "hints at closure" - no source found confirms an actual closure or cancelled 2026-27 season. Flagging as build/verified on best current evidence, but this is the single most likely Maine entry to have changed status by the time a later wave checks it; re-verify operating status and ownership before publishing.

areas.name: Pinnacle Ski Club
areas.note: Small community area in Pittsfield, Somerset County, operating continuously since 1954-55 with two rope tows and night skiing, no snowmaking. Despite the club name, tickets are sold to the public ($20 adult weekend day ticket, $40 season pass for 2025-26) per newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/pinnacle.php.

areas.name: Pleasant Mountain
areas.note: Operated under this name by Boyne Resorts since September 14, 2022, after being known as Shawnee Peak from 1988-2022 (Boyne acquired the property in October 2021). Located in Bridgton, Cumberland County, per Wikipedia (Pleasant Mountain Ski Area article). A later research wave should use "Pleasant Mountain" as the current operating name, not the older "Shawnee Peak" name still common in older sources.

areas.name: Powderhouse Hill
areas.note: Small area in South Berwick, York County, run by the town recreation department (absorbed into it in 2009 to keep it insured/operating), with a single rope tow dating to 1938. Confirmed open for 2025-26 (Dec 3 - Mar 8, $5 day ticket) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/powderhousehill.php.

areas.name: Quarry Road Trails
areas.note: Primarily a nordic/biathlon trail center in Waterville, Kennebec County, but per newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/quarryroad.php it also runs a lift-served alpine slope (a 400-foot portable rope tow installed circa 2021, on a snowmaking-covered pitch), which is why this is a build row rather than the Nordic-only drop rows below. A later wave should confirm the alpine tow is still running before writing guide copy, since it is a small secondary feature of a mostly-Nordic facility.

areas.name: Quoggy Jo Ski Area
areas.note: Community area off Fort Road in Presque Isle, Aroostook County, run by the Quoggy Jo Ski Club (control reverted to the club circa 2014 after Maine Winter Sports Center exited alpine skiing) with support from the Presque Isle Rotary Club. Single T-bar. Listed open for 2025-26 (Jan 7 - Mar 4, $275 season pass) via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/quoggyjo.php, though the same source documents a history of funding troubles (2022 funding-loss and near-closure news items) - a later wave should re-check this is still running before publishing.

areas.name: Saddleback Maine
areas.note: Base area sits in Sandy River Plantation, Franklin County, near but not within the town of Rangeley (confirmed via Wikipedia: "Saddleback Mountain is a mountain located in Sandy River Plantation, Franklin County, Maine, near the resort town of Rangeley"). Mailing address uses Rangeley, ME 04970 (saddlebackmaine.com). Operating for 2026-27; GM Jim Quimby has announced this will be his last season, per saddlebackmaine.com.

areas.name: Spruce Mountain
areas.note: Volunteer-run community area; the ski area's own site (sprucemountainmaine.wordpress.com, redirected from sprucemountain.org) states it is "jointly owned by the towns of Jay, Livermore, and Livermore Falls," but newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/sprucemtn.php establishes Jay, Maine (Franklin County) as the operating town of record, noting the town of Jay purchased the property from the Dion family in December 1987. Listed open for 2025-26 ($35 weekend ticket, Dec 26 - Mar 12) though the ski-history page itself was last substantively updated in 2016 - a later wave should reconfirm current operating status directly with the area (sprucemountainmaine.wordpress.com, @skispruce).

areas.name: Sugarloaf
areas.note: Operated by Boyne Resorts, currently operating. Confirmed via Wikipedia (Sugarloaf ski resort article: location Carrabassett Valley, Franklin County; status Operating; owner Boyne Resorts).

areas.name: Sunday River
areas.note: Operated by Boyne Resorts (acquired with Sugarloaf from American Skiing Company in 2007), currently operating. Confirmed via Wikipedia (Sunday River ski resort article: town Newry, Oxford County).

areas.name: Titcomb Mountain
areas.note: Non-profit community area operated by the Farmington Ski Club, Farmington, Franklin County. Confirmed operating 2025-26, with a lift-construction update reported January 2026, via newenglandskihistory.com/Maine/titcomb.php.

areas.name: Berkshire East Ski Resort
areas.note: Base area in Charlemont, Franklin County; terrain also extends into neighboring Hawley (also Franklin County). Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Berkshire East Ski Resort), status listed 'Active' with 2025-2026 chairlift/ownership updates (Bear Den Partners).

areas.name: Blue Hills Ski Area
areas.note: Sits within Blue Hills Reservation (Commonwealth land) in Canton, Norfolk County, with the ski operation run as a concession similar to Wachusett. Confirmed via Wikipedia (Blue Hills Ski Area); official site listed as bluehillsboston.com.

areas.name: Bousquet Mountain
areas.note: Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Bousquet Mountain), status 'Operating', owned by Mill Town Capital since May 2020 with ongoing facility upgrades.

areas.name: Catamount Ski Area
areas.note: Straddles the MA/NY state line; one base lodge is in South Egremont (town of Egremont), Berkshire County, MA, the other in Hillsdale, Columbia County, NY. Confirmed via Wikipedia (Catamount Ski Area, status 'Operating') and operator site catamountski.com, which references Winter 26/27 season passes. The area straddles the Massachusetts/New York line. No decisive anchor was found for the base lodge's state -- no distinguishing address or licence jurisdiction turned up -- but Wikipedia's Egremont, MA article says the ski area IS SITED there, while its Hillsdale, NY article says only that the area is NEAR Hillsdale. That asymmetry is real evidence, short of certainty, so this row is filed to Massachusetts on that basis. The base-lodge state is not conclusively sourced, and a later content wave must name New York in prose.

areas.name: Jiminy Peak
areas.note: Base area and main lodge in Hancock, Berkshire County; summit facilities (Hendricks Summit Lodge) extend into neighboring Lanesborough. Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Jiminy Peak (ski area)), page updated August 2026, owned by Sculptor Capital Management, operated by Brian Fairbank.

areas.name: Nashoba Valley Ski Area
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia (Nashoba Valley Ski Area), operating continuously since opening in 1964, official site skinashoba.com.

areas.name: Otis Ridge
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia (Otis Ridge) and operator site (otisridge.com, address 159 Monterey Road, Otis, MA), which advertises 26/27 season passes. Owned by Ski Butternut since 2016 after a foreclosure rescue.

areas.name: Ski Bradford
areas.note: Located in the Bradford section of Haverhill, Essex County. Confirmed via operator site skibradford.com (address 60 S Cross Rd, Haverhill, MA 01835), which as of the September 2026 fetch was in off-season and stated it plans to reopen for the 2026/27 season with public lift tickets, and via Wikipedia (Ski Bradford).

areas.name: Ski Butternut
areas.note: On Warner Mountain in Great Barrington, Berkshire County. Confirmed via Wikipedia (Ski Butternut) and corroborated by skicentral.com Massachusetts listing. This operator also owns Otis Ridge and formerly owned Blandford Ski Area.

areas.name: Ski Ward
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia (Ski Ward) and operator site (skiward.com, 1000 Main Street, Shrewsbury, MA); in continuous operation since 1939.

areas.name: Wachusett Mountain
areas.note: Operates under a lease within Wachusett Mountain State Reservation, which is Commonwealth land; the ski area itself is privately operated. Confirmed operating via Wikipedia (Wachusett Mountain (ski area)) and task-supplied example.

areas.name: Abenaki Ski Area
areas.note: Town-of-Wolfeboro-owned community hill with a published public lift ticket; listed in the current Ski NH member directory as 'Abenaki Ski Area - Wolfeboro, NH,' and Wikipedia's Wolfeboro, NH article confirms the town is in Carroll County.

areas.name: Arrowhead Recreation Area
areas.note: Small community area; Wikipedia's Arrowhead Recreation Area article confirms it reopened in 2002, runs a rope tow for alpine skiing and tubing (lit for night operations), and is located in Claremont, Sullivan County.

areas.name: Attitash Mountain Resort
areas.note: Confirmed operating; Ski New Hampshire member directory (skinh.com/resorts) and Wikipedia's Bartlett, NH article both place it in Bartlett, Carroll County.

areas.name: Black Mountain
areas.note: Had announced a possible 2023-24 closure over costs/staffing but reversed and kept operating; per Wikipedia (Black Mountain (New Hampshire)), owner Erik Mogensen purchased it outright in March 2026 and is investing further in it as an independent-ski-area laboratory, so it is operating for 2026-27. Located in Jackson, Carroll County per the same source.

areas.name: Bretton Woods
areas.note: Ski NH lists this as 'Bretton Woods, NH' but Bretton Woods is an unincorporated village, not a town; Wikipedia's Carroll, NH article confirms Bretton Woods is a village within the incorporated town of Carroll, Coos County, and identifies the Mount Washington Hotel/Bretton Woods resort area as being within Carroll.

areas.name: Cannon Mountain
areas.note: State-owned, operated by NH Division of Parks and Recreation within Franconia Notch State Park. Wikipedia's Franconia, NH article confirms the town of Franconia (Grafton County) contains the northern half of Franconia Notch State Park and the Cannon Mountain Aerial Tramway; carries an aerial tramway.

areas.name: Cranmore Mountain Resort
areas.note: Ski NH lists it as North Conway, but Wikipedia's Conway, NH article states the resort is 'in Conway' (the town), Carroll County -- North Conway is a village within the town, not a separate municipality.

areas.name: Crotched Mountain Ski & Ride
areas.note: Sits on the Bennington/Francestown town line; Wikipedia's Bennington, NH article states the town 'is the home of ... Crotched Mountain Ski & Ride,' and the Wikipedia article on the ski area itself and Tripadvisor both list the base as Bennington, Hillsborough County, even though the summit sits on Francestown's western border and Ski NH's own directory labels it Francestown. Vail Resorts-owned (Peak Resorts era). Town corrected from Bennington to Francestown: Ski New Hampshire's official member directory gives the published base-lodge address as 615 Francestown Road, Francestown, NH 03442 (skinh.com/resorts/crotched-mountain). Many sources say Bennington because the historical land purchase and the western slopes sit there, and Wikipedia's Bennington, NH article describes the resort as sitting "on the Francestown line" -- but the summit and the current base area are in Francestown, and that is what decides the town field here. Hillsborough County is unchanged.

areas.name: Dartmouth Skiway
areas.note: Owned by Dartmouth College but open to the public with a published lift ticket; Ski NH directory lists it as 'Lyme Center, NH' -- Lyme Center is a village within the incorporated town of Lyme, Grafton County.

areas.name: Granite Gorge Ski Area
areas.note: Wikipedia's Granite Gorge Ski Area article lists operating status as 'Operating,' located in Roxbury, Cheshire County (also confirmed by Wikipedia's Roxbury, NH article).

areas.name: Gunstock Mountain Resort
areas.note: County-owned (Belknap County recreation area); Wikipedia's Gilford, NH article confirms the resort is in Gilford, Belknap County.

areas.name: King Pine Ski Area
areas.note: Located at Purity Spring Resort in the East Madison village; Ski NH lists it as East Madison, NH and Wikipedia's Madison, NH article confirms 'King Pine Ski Area at Purity Spring Resort' is a site of interest in Madison, Carroll County. East Madison is a village, not a separate town.

areas.name: Loon Mountain Resort
areas.note: Boyne-owned resort; Ski NH directory and general NH municipal geography confirm the base is in Lincoln, Grafton County.

areas.name: McIntyre Ski Area
areas.note: City-of-Manchester-owned community hill with published public lift tickets; listed in the current Ski NH member directory as 'McIntyre Ski Area - Manchester, NH,' which is in Hillsborough County.

areas.name: Mount Eustis Ski Hill
areas.note: Non-profit community ski hill at 188 Mt. Eustis Road, Littleton NH, rope-tow served with night skiing. Reopened Feb 7, 2015 after a 32-year closure; organized as a 501(c) non-profit ("Mt. Eustis Ski Hill") in 2013. Operator's own site (mteustis.org) documents a completed 2025-26 season (24 lift-served operating days, closed March 25, 2026, "see you next winter"), with mission language describing low/no-cost community access rather than a residents-only or members-only restriction. Absent from the New Hampshire research file's build and drop lists entirely, and not in the Ski NH member directory (which only covers larger dues-paying members) -- exactly the roster blind spot this sweep was built to catch.

areas.name: Mount Sunapee Resort
areas.note: State-owned (Mount Sunapee State Park), operated under lease by Vail Resorts. Wikipedia's Mount Sunapee Resort article confirms the base is in Newbury, Merrimack County (not the separate town of Sunapee, which is in Sullivan County).

areas.name: Pat's Peak
areas.note: Family-owned; Ski NH directory and general NH municipal geography place Henniker in Merrimack County.

areas.name: Ragged Mountain Resort
areas.note: Wikipedia's Ragged Mountain Resort article confirms the base is in Danbury (not the more commonly associated Andover), Merrimack County.

areas.name: Storrs Hill Ski Area
areas.note: City-of-Lebanon-owned community hill; Wikipedia's Lebanon, NH article (present tense, current revision) confirms the city maintains 'a municipal ski area' among its recreational facilities in Grafton County. Could not independently re-confirm the specific lift type or a dated 2026-27 season announcement via the city's own site (repeated fetch attempts to lebanonnh.gov 404'd), so treat the operating-season particulars as needing a follow-up check even though the facility's existence and town/county are solid.

areas.name: Tenney Mountain
areas.note: Had a long closure (2010-2023) and NELSAP's page is stale on this point, but onthesnow.com's live ski report confirms current seasonal operation ('Closed for the season, projected reopening Dec 05'), and Wikipedia's Tenney Mountain Ski Resort article confirms lift-served skiing resumed Feb 2023 under North Country Development Group, with the base in Plymouth, Grafton County (the mountain's summit is technically over the line in Rumney/Groton).

areas.name: Waterville Valley Resort
areas.note: Wikipedia's Waterville Valley, NH article confirms it is an incorporated town (Grafton County) that contains the resort -- one of the rare cases where the resort town itself is the incorporated municipality.

areas.name: Whaleback Mountain
areas.note: Non-profit community area run by the Upper Valley Snow Sports Foundation since 2013; Wikipedia's Whaleback (ski area) article confirms it operated through the 2024-25 season and is located in Enfield, Grafton County.

areas.name: Wildcat Mountain
areas.note: Ski NH's directory labels it 'Gorham, NH,' but Wikipedia's Pinkham's Grant article states the ski area's base is in the eastern part of Pinkham's Grant, an unincorporated township in Coos County entirely within the White Mountain National Forest -- not the town of Gorham. Base lodge on NH Route 16 in Pinkham Notch.

areas.name: Yawgoo Valley
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia (Yawgoo Valley), described as 'the only surviving skiing resort in Rhode Island,' located in Exeter, Washington County; operates 2 chairlifts and 1 rope tow with published public lift ticket pricing. This is the sole operating lift-served ski area found in Rhode Island; the state's near-total lack of other areas is expected, not a sign of missed research.

areas.name: Ascutney Outdoors
areas.note: Nonprofit successor to the former commercial Ascutney Mountain Resort (closed 2010); community-purchased in 2015 and now runs a public lift. Confirmed via Wikipedia (Ascutney Mountain Resort / West Windsor articles); village of Brownsville is within the town of West Windsor, Windsor County.

areas.name: Bolton Valley Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; town of Bolton, Chittenden County. NELSAP lists it among areas that closed and successfully reopened.

areas.name: Bromley Mountain Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; town of Peru, Bennington County, east of Manchester.

areas.name: Burke Mountain Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia ("Burke Mountain Ski Area"); base near the village of East Burke, within the town of Burke, Caledonia County.

areas.name: Cochran's Ski Area
areas.note: Nonprofit, volunteer-run community ski area founded by the Cochran ski-racing family; operator's own site (cochranskiarea.com) confirms public day tickets and address at 910 Cochran Road, Richmond, Chittenden County.

areas.name: Hard'Ack
areas.note: Municipal/volunteer-run rope-tow and tubing hill. Listed as "still open" in NELSAP's currently-operating small-areas roundup and in Wikipedia's Vermont ski-areas list. Municipality confirmed via OpenStreetMap/Nominatim as Saint Albans City, Franklin County (operator site hardack.org could not be reached this session due to an expired TLS certificate).

areas.name: Harrington Hill
areas.note: Small community rope-tow hill run by the Strafford Lions Club; listed as "still open" in NELSAP's currently-operating small-areas roundup, and named in Wikipedia's list of Vermont ski areas. Town of Strafford confirmed to be in Orange County via Wikipedia.

areas.name: Jay Peak Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; base area primarily in the town of Jay, Orleans County.

areas.name: Killington Ski Resort
areas.note: Confirmed operating via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; base area is in the town of Killington, Rutland County.

areas.name: Living Memorial Park
areas.note: Town-owned recreation area; Wikipedia's Brattleboro article describes it as containing "a municipal skiing facility," and NELSAP lists it among areas that reopened. Town of Brattleboro, Windham County.

areas.name: Lyndon Outing Club
areas.note: Community-run hill on Shonya Hill. The Town of Lyndon's own website currently lists "downhill skiing... at Lyndon Outing Club" among local recreation, and NELSAP's currently-operating small-areas roundup lists it as "still open." Lyndonville village is within the town of Lyndon, Caledonia County.

areas.name: Mad River Glen
areas.note: Co-operatively owned (member/shareholder model). Confirmed via Ski Vermont mountain finder and general reference sources; town of Fayston, Washington County.

areas.name: Magic Mountain
areas.note: Confirmed via operator site (magicmtn.com, address in Londonderry) and Wikipedia's Londonderry article listing it as a local attraction; Windham County. NELSAP notes it reopened after a prior closure.

areas.name: Middlebury College Snow Bowl
areas.note: Owned and operated by Middlebury College but confirmed open to the general public via day tickets/season passes on the operator's own site (middleburysnowbowl.com); base address in Hancock, Addison County per Wikipedia.

areas.name: Mount Snow
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia infobox ("Dover, Windham County, Vermont"); the resort's public-facing address uses the village name West Dover, within the town of Dover.

areas.name: Northeast Slopes
areas.note: Nonprofit community rope-tow hill; operator's own site (northeastslopes.org) confirms public lift-ticket pricing and weekend operating hours. Village of East Corinth is within the town of Corinth, Orange County (confirmed via Wikipedia).

areas.name: Okemo Mountain Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; base area on Ludlow Mountain in the town of Ludlow, Windsor County.

areas.name: Pico Mountain
areas.note: Sister mountain to Killington under common ownership. Wikipedia places the base area in the town of Killington, just inside the Mendon town line, Rutland County.

areas.name: Saskadena Six
areas.note: Formerly known as Suicide Six; confirmed via Wikipedia's Pomfret article, which describes the resort at South Pomfret (a village within the town of Pomfret), Windsor County. Owned/operated in connection with the Woodstock Inn.

areas.name: Smugglers' Notch Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia; resort sits in the town of Cambridge near the village of Jeffersonville, Lamoille County.

areas.name: Stowe Mountain Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; town of Stowe, Lamoille County.

areas.name: Stratton Mountain Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia; located on Stratton Mountain in the town of Stratton, Windham County (east of Manchester).

areas.name: Sugarbush Resort
areas.note: Confirmed via Wikipedia and Ski Vermont mountain finder; located in the Mad River Valley, town of Warren, Washington County.
